title: 502 Bad Gateway after a "successful" deploy

source.title: 502 bad gateway after last update (Ghost Forum)

brief:
**#deploys 14:02 · api-01 · shop-api 2.4 rolled out, pipeline green**

> "Pipeline is green, `systemctl is-active shop-api` says active. Ship it!"

**14:04:** the shop's frontend reports **502 Bad Gateway** from `api.shop.example.com`. nginx on this box proxies to shop-api, a small Python service started by systemd.

The app is running, and nginx is running too. The fault is in how they meet. Use nginx's error log, `ss` and the app's own settings to find where the request goes and where the app actually listens. After that, the finance team has a second complaint about the monthly report. Keep the site's fail-fast timeout (ticket SRE-88) for everything else.

tasks.title: Find where the request goes
tasks.text:
A **502** means nginx couldn't get a usable answer from its upstream, here because the connection itself failed. `sudo tail /var/log/nginx/error.log` names the exact upstream address nginx tried. `sudo ss -ltn` shows what is really listening. `/etc/shop-api/env` and the release note in it explain why they differ.

Make them meet: change the proxy, or change the app, but test with `nginx -t` before a reload. Done when `curl -H 'Host: api.shop.example.com' http://127.0.0.1/` answers 200 with shop-api's JSON.
hints: The error log says `connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, ... upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:2368/"`, and `ss -ltn` shows `127.0.0.1:2369`. Test the backend directly: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:2369/`.
In `/etc/nginx/sites-available/shop-api` change the upstream to `server 127.0.0.1:2369;`, then `sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx`.

questions.prompt: Which port does shop-api 2.4 actually listen on?
Which error text, after "111:", does nginx log for this 502?

checks.describe: nginx -t passes; nginx and shop-api run and start at boot; / answers 200 with shop-api's JSON

tasks.title: The report that times out
tasks.text:
Now try `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' -H 'Host: api.shop.example.com' http://127.0.0.1/reports/monthly`. A different 5xx, after about 3 seconds. The app is up; it just needs about 5 seconds for this report.

Raise the limit for the report location only. The 3-second limit protects the rest of the API from hung requests, and a monitoring probe, `/api/stall`, checks that it still applies. Done when the report answers 200 and `/api/stall` still fails fast.
hints: The error log says `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header`. `sudo nginx -T | grep -n timeout` shows the server-wide `proxy_read_timeout 3s;`.

Add a `location /reports/ { proxy_pass http://shop_api; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_read_timeout 30s; }` above `location /`, then `sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx`. Don't change the server-wide 3s.

questions.prompt: Which status code does nginx return when the upstream accepts the connection but answers too slowly?
Which nginx directive sets how long nginx waits for the upstream's response?

checks.describe: /reports/monthly answers 200; /api/stall still gets a fast 504; no proxy_read_timeout above 300 s

walkthrough:
### What was broken
1. shop-api 2.4 changed its default port from 2368 to 2369 (`/etc/shop-api/env`). The unit was active, so the pipeline's "is it running?" check passed, but nginx still sent requests to `127.0.0.1:2368`, where nothing listens: `connect() failed (111: Connection refused)` → **502**.
2. The server block sets `proxy_read_timeout 3s` for every location. `/reports/monthly` needs about 5 s, so nginx gave up first: `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)` → **504**.

### Task 1
```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Host: api.shop.example.com' http://127.0.0.1/   # 502
sudo tail -2 /var/log/nginx/error.log      # (111: Connection refused) ... upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:2368/"
sudo ss -ltn                               # 127.0.0.1:2369
cat /etc/shop-api/env                      # PORT=2369
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:2369/             # the app answers directly
sudo sed -i 's/127.0.0.1:2368/127.0.0.1:2369/' /etc/nginx/sites-available/shop-api
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
```
*Read the 5xx:* **502** means the connection failed or the upstream sent garbage (wrong port, app down, app bound to another address). **504** means it connected but the answer took longer than `proxy_read_timeout`. The same split applies to Traefik, Dokploy and Coolify: a "port mismatch" or an app listening on `127.0.0.1` inside its container both give 502.

### Task 2
```nginx
    location /reports/ {
        proxy_pass http://shop_api;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_read_timeout 30s;
    }
```
```bash
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
curl -s -w ' %{http_code} %{time_total}\n' -H 'Host: api.shop.example.com' http://127.0.0.1/reports/monthly   # 200, ~5 s
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' -H 'Host: api.shop.example.com' http://127.0.0.1/api/stall   # 504, ~3 s
```
*Why per location:* directives in a `location` override the server-level value only there. Pick a limit a little above the slowest real request, not hours. The real fix for a slow report is to make it asynchronous (start a job, poll for the result).

**Source (adapted):** [502 bad gateway after last update (Ghost Forum)](https://forum.ghost.org/t/502-bad-gateway-after-last-update/19294): after an update, nginx logged `connect() failed (111: Connection refused)` for `127.0.0.1:2368`. `netstat -plant` showed Ghost on 2369, and correcting the port in the nginx configs fixed it. The 504 timeout task is added.
